title: Local models of integral constructible complexes and their cohomology
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k_0$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite extension, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and a chosen uniformizer $\pi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Use the completed coefficient sheaf $\mathcal O_{E,X}$ of [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] and the bounded-constructible cohomology definition of $\Dbc$ in [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Let $K\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$.

1. There is a finite stratification of $X$ such that on each stratum $S$,
   pro-étale locally on $S$, $K|_S$ is the completion
   $\widehat{\underline{M^\bullet}}=M^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_{E,S}$
   of a bounded complex $M^\bullet$ of finite free $\mathcal O_E$-modules, with
   differentials given by matrices over $\mathcal O_E$.
2. Each cohomology sheaf $H^q(K)$ is derived complete, lies in
   $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$, and on each stratum of (1) is pro-étale locally the
   completion of the finitely generated $\mathcal O_E$-module $H^q(M^\bullet)$.
3. Every truncation $\tau_{\le q}K$, $\tau_{\ge q}K$ lies in
   $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$.

proof.text: Put $R=\mathcal O_E$, $\pi=\pi_E$, $k=R/(\pi)$ and $B_T=\mathcal O_{E,T}$. Use the Noetherian scheme setting and the identification $B_T=\varprojlim_n(R/\pi^n)_T$ in [sk-lem-integral-models]. The coefficient hypotheses for the stratified-perfect theorem applied in step 2 hold with $A=R$ and $I=(\pi)$: [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] makes $R$ a local PID, hence Noetherian since each ideal has one generator. Here is also the elementary completeness check, rather than an unstated change of coefficient topology. For a compatible sequence of residue classes choose representatives $a_n\in R$. For $m\ge n$, $a_m-a_n\in\pi^nR$, hence $|a_m-a_n|_E\le|\pi|_E^n\to0$. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-complete] they converge to $a\in E$. The nonarchimedean inequality of [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value] shows $a\in R$ and $a-a_n\in\pi^nR$: both assertions follow by passing to the limit in the corresponding closed-ball inequality, using the DVR factorization to identify the ball of radius $|\pi|_E^n$ with $\pi^nR$. Thus $R\to\varprojlim R/\pi^n$ is onto. It is injective because $|a|_E\le|\pi|_E^n$ for all $n$ forces $a=0$.

source.place: Clause (1), coefficient hypotheses for the adic local-structure theorem

proof.text: The meaning of $K\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ is boundedness with constructible cohomology in [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Apply (1)$\Rightarrow$(2) of [lem-sfb-integral-cohomological-adic-criterion] to this $B_X$-complex. It gives locally derived $(\pi)$-completeness and an isomorphism $K\otimes^L_{B_X}k_X\simeq\nu_X^*C$, with $C$ bounded étale constructible of finite Tor amplitude. These are exactly condition (a) of [lem-sfb-adic-stratified-perfect], not just a residue sheaf constancy assumption. Its implication (a)$\Rightarrow$(b), with the ring hypotheses checked in step 1, gives a finite constructible locally closed stratification of $X$ and on a pro-étale cover of each stratum $S$ an isomorphism $K|_S\simeq B_S\otimes_R P^\bullet$ for a bounded complex of finite projective $R$-modules. The theorem itself identifies the restricted coefficient with $B_S$ and supplies the stratification and the scalar-ring complex. No claim that arbitrary maps between completed free sheaves have constant entries is used.

For each term of $P^\bullet$ from step 2, finite projectivity gives a split surjection $R^r\twoheadrightarrow P^i$: choose finitely many generators, and split this surjection by projectivity. Thus $P^i$ embeds into $R^r$; since $R$ is a domain by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], it is torsion-free. Apply [lem-sc-dvr-fg-torsionfree-free] to obtain a finite $R$-basis of each $P^i$. There are only finitely many nonzero terms. In these bases each $R$-linear differential is a finite matrix over $R$; conjugating consecutive differentials preserves their zero composite. The resulting bounded finite free $R$-complex $M^\bullet$ is isomorphic to $P^\bullet$, so $B_S\otimes_R M^\bullet$ is the required local model in (1). This is freeness of modules over $R$, not a freeness or constancy assertion about projectors over the sheaf $B_S$.

source.place: Clause (1), finite free models over the discrete valuation ring; Stacks Tag 0AUW(3)

proof.text: Fix $q$. By [sk-def-sfb-constructible], $H^q(K)$ is already a constructible $B_X$-module sheaf. As a degree-zero complex it has only this cohomology sheaf, so it is bounded with constructible cohomology (the other sheaves are zero, with the zero finite constant model). It therefore belongs to $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$. Now [sk-lem-integral-models](2) says explicitly that objects of this $\Dbc$ are derived complete, with derived completeness defined in its setup by the canonical isomorphism to the derived limit of reductions. Apply it to $H^q(K)[0]$. This proves derived completeness in the precise sense of [sk-def-pe-derived-completion] used here; no identification of that definition with local internal-Hom completeness is required here. This argument is independent of the local cohomology computation below and does not interchange cohomology and an inverse limit.

source.place: Clause (2), *Completeness*; realized by sk-lem-integral-models(2) applied to the degree-zero object H^q(K)[0] instead of Stacks Tags 0990 and 099Q(5)

proof.text: Use exactly the stratification and charts of steps 2–3. The exact inverse-image functor with its coefficient identification in [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] commutes with cohomology: it preserves the kernels and images defining cohomology, both for restriction to $S$ and for the pro-étale charts. On such a chart $U$ the constant-sheaf functor on $R$-modules is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-module-section-properties](1). The completed coefficient $B_U=\varprojlim_n(R/\pi^n)_U$ is flat over the constant sheaf $\underline R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction]. The composite functor $N\mapsto B_U\otimes_{\underline R}\underline N$ is therefore exact. Apply it to the cycles, boundaries and their short exact sequences in $M^\bullet$ to obtain $H^q(K)|_U\simeq B_U\otimes_R H^q(M^\bullet)$. This is the completed module $\widehat{\underline{H^q(M^\bullet)}}$, computed by extension of scalars, not by commuting an inverse limit with cohomology. Finally $\ker(d^q)\subset M^q$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite], since $R$ is Noetherian by step 1. Its quotient $\ker(d^q)/\operatorname{im}(d^{q-1})=H^q(M^\bullet)$ is finite, because the images of a finite generating set generate any quotient. Together with step 4 this proves every assertion of (2), on the original strata of (1).

source.place: Clause (2), local cohomology of finite free models; Stacks Tags 093J, 093M, 00IK

proof.text: Choose a finite cohomological interval $[a,b]$ for $K$. By the good-truncation formulas in [def-kun-truncations], the cohomology sheaves of $\tau_{\le q}K$ are $H^i(K)$ for $i\le q$ and zero for $i>q$, and those of $\tau_{\ge q}K$ are $H^i(K)$ for $i\ge q$ and zero for $i<q$. Each list vanishes outside $[a,b]$ and consists of constructible sheaves: this holds for $H^i(K)$ by hypothesis and for zero by its zero finite constant model. Thus both truncations are bounded with constructible cohomology, which is precisely membership in $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ by [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. This proves (3) directly in $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$, without identifying it with a separately defined adic category.

source.place: Clause (3), elementary truncation argument using the bounded-constructible definition

Replaced the invalid constancy argument by the existing complete-local-ring stratified-perfect theorem after the category-correct integral criterion; specialized finite projective scalar modules to free modules explicitly. Derived completeness of H^q in the derived-limit sense is obtained by applying sk-lem-integral-models(2) to its constructible degree-zero object; the local H^q computation now cites coefficient flatness and exact restriction. Truncation membership follows directly from bounded constructible cohomology. No statement change or new nodes. reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q46-192066148 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item, the unit and the blueprint statement and proof, and the statements of all 14 cited nodes. I also checked Bhatt–Scholze Definition 6.5.1, Example 6.5.2, Lemma 6.5.3 and Proposition 6.6.11 (with its proof), and Stacks Tag 093M (sites-modules.tex line 8261). The three conclusions match the blueprint word for word. The added opening fixes the chapter's standard setting, the same one used in sk-def-sfb-dc-setting and sk-lem-integral-models. It closes a statement that left X and E undefined and weakens nothing for the four nodes that cite this item; this is not a target node. Step 1: O_E is a DVR, hence Noetherian, local and π-adically complete; the elementary completeness proof is correct. Step 2: condition (1) of lem-sfb-integral-cohomological-adic-criterion uses the same constructibility as sk-def-sfb-constructible. Its condition (2) matches condition (a) of lem-sfb-adic-stratified-perfect with A=O_E and I=(π): the same local completeness notion and the same finite Tor amplitude. Going from (a) to (b) gives the strata and a finite projective scalar complex. This agrees with Bhatt–Scholze 6.6.11 and no longer assumes the Tag 09C3 differentials are constant. Step 3: a finite projective module over a domain is torsion-free, and lem-sc-dvr-fg-torsionfree-free then makes it free. Step 4: H^q(K)[0] lies in Dbc by definition, and sk-lem-integral-models(2) gives derived completeness in the derived-limit sense; this is not circular. Step 5: restriction is exact (sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients), taking constant sheaves is exact (Tag 093J), and B is flat over the constant sheaf (Tag 093M), so H^q of the local model is B⊗H^q(M); H^q(M) is finitely generated by Tag 00IK. Step 6: the good-truncation formulas give the result directly. Small cases checked: the empty scheme, a geometric point, O_E/π[0] modelled by the complex O_E --π--> O_E (torsion H^0), shifts, and truncation indices outside the range. There are no new nodes. No dependency path leads back to the item (I traversed 3119 nodes), and no SGA source is used. I accept the declared tool uses as generic black-box tools; none replaces a step of the unit's route.
